title: Why Barber Poles Are Red and White

sections.name: Why Barber Poles Are Red and White
lines: Ever wondered why barber poles have red and white stripes? It's a pretty dark story.
For centuries, barbers didn't just cut hair. They pulled teeth, set bones, and did surgery.
Their most common job was bloodletting. The patient squeezed a pole to make their veins stand out.
Afterwards, so the story goes, the bandages were washed and hung outside on that pole to dry.
As they twisted in the wind, they formed a spiral. Red and white.
That spiral became the barber's sign. The blue stripe was added later, in America.
